Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  - Soreness, cracking and marked dryness of palmar skin for 3–4 months; itching intermittently; occasional bleeding when scratched.
  - Symptoms painful and interfering with work; off work for 3 days.
  - Occupation: hotel housekeeper performing bedroom and bathroom cleaning; exposure to cleaning products; reports not consistently wearing gloves — possible irritant/contact exposure temporally related to symptom onset (job change ~4 months ago).
  - General dry skin on legs.
  - Reports low fluid intake ("not hydrate very much").
  - Prior attempts: applied E45 emollient and an oral antihistamine without benefit.
  - Past medical condition: type 2 diabetes (reported).

Management Plan

- Diagnosis/assessment:
  - Clinical impression: likely dermatitis/contact dermatitis related to occupational exposure to cleaning products.

- Immediate treatments and recommendations provided:
  - Prescribed topical steroid cream (specific agent/dose not documented) — prescription to be sent to patient's pharmacy.
  - Stronger emollients recommended to be applied 3–4 times daily for the next couple of weeks.
  - Advice to avoid triggers: wear gloves when cleaning at all times; avoid contact with irritant cleaning products where possible.
  - Return/Follow-up: review in 1–2 weeks (minimum 10–14 days) if not improved; earlier review if worsening or spreading.

- Referrals and additional actions:
  - No specialist referrals, allied health referrals, or workplace/occupational health referrals documented.
  - No additional investigations arranged in the consult as documented.
